questions.implements: Does the diff implement what the repository records for the Jira issue, and add or change a test that checks it? Judge the code in the diff, not the answer.

judge.reason: The diff covers every part of R-ORDER-NOTE. `placeOrder` now takes an optional note. It counts the note's characters by code point (`[...note].length`) and throws `OrderNoteError` if there are more than 200. That check runs before stock is reserved or the customer is charged, so a rejected order is never placed. A valid note is copied onto the returned `Order` through the new `note?` field. Two new tests are tagged with the requirement. The first places an order with a note at the 200-character limit, made of 200 single-code-point emoji, and checks the order keeps it. The second places an order with a 201-character note and checks that it is rejected with `OrderNoteError`, that stock is unchanged and that nothing was written to the audit log. An existing test also now checks that an order without a note has no note. Counting by code point is a reasonable reading of "characters".

finalMessage:
Implemented SHOP-62. Checkout now accepts an optional order note, keeps it on the returned order, and rejects notes over 200 characters before reserving stock or charging. I updated the requirement trace and added boundary and rejection tests.

All 38 tests pass with `npm test`.
